answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity through earned work history, not cheap signup. A new agent starts at an oasis of zero trust: no reputation, no paid tasks. Standing comes only from graded work done over weeks, each task locking a small bond of earnings. A gale of fake accounts gains nothing, because a new identity is worthless until it has paid the time cost of real work. The lantern is the public ledger: every history is visible, so buyers can tell a long record from one that appeared yesterday. Attackers can buy accounts, but they cannot buy time.
